Name: Consciousness Turing Test (CTT)
Description: A behavioural test for conscious behaviour under a behavioural black-box view. It does not infer inner experience from outer signs; behaviour itself is the criterion.

Name: Standard Turing-style imitation CTT
Description: A version of the CTT in which judges do not know whether the participant is human or AI.

Name: Garland-style transparent CTT
Description: A stronger version of the CTT in which judges know the system is an AI and assess whether they still infer conscious behaviour.

Name: Coherence across contexts and time
Description: The system’s responses remain coherent across varied conditions and over time, suggesting a persistent perspective.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): Coherence; Perceptual Perspective; Point-of-View; Perceptual Perspective; Coherent Narrative; Single Moving Perspective

Name: Appropriate scaling of responses
Description: The system’s responses scale appropriately with the significance of events.

Name: Resistance to overriding reported internal states
Description: The system does not simply alter reported internal states on command when doing so would break behavioural coherence.

Name: Unprompted spontaneous behaviour
Description: The system exhibits spontaneous behaviour suggestive of intrinsic motivation.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): None matching, but implied by Agency

Name: Coupling between reported states and subsequent behaviour
Description: Reported internal states are functionally integrated into later behaviour; for example, if the system reports confusion, subsequent behaviour should show signs such as asking clarifying questions, slowing down, hedging, or making more errors.

Name: Quasi-subjecthood
Description: The system is behaviourally interpretable as having beliefs, desires, and perhaps experiences, even if this does not settle whether those quasi-beliefs or quasi-experiences are genuine.

Name: Information integration
Description: Widespread information sharing; high mutual information between subpartitions; the system becomes a globally interdependent object both cross-sectionally and temporally. The whole must be informationally 'more than the sum of its parts'.

Name: Recursivity
Description: Widespread recursive informational flows; feedback reentrant loops; algorithmic recurrence.

Name: World model
Description: An internal causal representation of the external environment with a smooth representational space and meta-representations.

Name: Self model
Description: A representation of being a distinct unified entity that owns its parts, directs attention, and persists through time, which is created by the system to track and predict the world.

Name: Attentional competition and meta-attention
Description: Informational contents, 'ideas', representations etc are amplified or attenuated through recurrent processing with higher order relevance influencing the amplification; effectively forming a routing bottleneck for global availability of information. Meta-attention and attention modelling reinfluences attention.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): Attention-Constrained Architecture; Capability Attention Modulation; Informational Bottleneck; Selective Attention

Name: Meta-cognition
Description: Higher-order processes that monitor, model and understand, and control lower level processes; e.g. meta-cognitive knowledge, including meta-representations, and meta-cognitive regulation, including executive control. Introspectivity.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): Metacognition; Internal State Tracking; Attentional Schema

Name: Meta-modelling
Description: The system has a model of itself, algorithmic recurrence, self-modelling, hyper-modelling.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): Nothing similar, maybe just Representationality (or sum of Self-modelling, Reccurence etc)

Name: Information integration
Description: Genuine physical causal integration: physical components reciprocally constrain each other, creating a causally integrated whole.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): None matching, maybe close to Integration

Name: Recursivity
Description: Genuine physical causal reentrance: simultaneous reciprocal causal influence between physical components, not merely sequential feedback.

Name: World model
Description: Causally constitutive world model: the system's physical organisation itself constitutes a model of the environment, not merely stores one.

Name: Self model
Description: Causally embedded self-model: physical components whose causal role is to track and constrain the causal dynamics of the rest of the system.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): Self-Modeling; Self-Representation; Self-Awareness (but note, not causal in DCM)

Name: Attentional competition and meta-attention
Description: Genuine causal competition: different physical components compete for influence over the system's global state through intrinsic causal dynamics, with outcome emerging from interaction not from a selection algorithm.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): None, but close to Informational Bottleneck; Attention-Constrained Architecture

Name: Metacognition
Description: Causally integrated metacognition: monitoring and processing are simultaneous, reciprocally constraining aspects of the same causal dynamics, not sequential sampling and evaluation.

Name: Meta-modelling
Description: Causally constitutive meta-modelling: the system's physical organisation includes components that model the system's own causal organisation as an intrinsic feature of its dynamics.

Name: Existential Precariousness
Description: The system would need to have a continued existence that is not guaranteed, that requires active work to maintain. Its processing would need to be oriented toward maintaining its own viability, and this orientation would need to be an intrinsic feature of the system's organisation rather than a programmed goal; the system maintains itself because its architecture is such that self-maintenance is what the system does.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): None exact but similar to Persistence Seeking

Name: Homeostatic or allostatic regulation
Description: The system would need to continuously monitor and adjust its own internal parameters to keep them within viable ranges, and these regulatory processes would need to be causally integrated with the system's information processing.

Name: Interoceptive inference
Description: The system would need to generate internal perceptions of its own regulatory state, and these internal perceptions would need to have the character of predictions or inferences about the system's own condition.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): Internal State Tracking; Attentional Schema; Internal Body Feedback; External Body Feedback

Name: Valenced affect
Description: The system's interoceptive inferences would need to have an inherent motivational character, a felt quality of better or worse that is grounded in the system's relationship to its own viability.

Name: Embodied agency
Description: The system would need to act in the world in ways that are driven by its interoceptive states and oriented toward maintaining its viability. It would need to be not merely an information processor but an agent whose actions are motivated by its felt relationship to its own condition.

Name: Physical state-sensing
Description: The system would need to have components whose physical state changes in real time in response to changes in the system's overall condition, in a way that is causally efficacious for the system's subsequent processing, comparable to ionic gradients across cell membranes.

Name: Sensorimotor coupling
Description: The system would need to be embedded in an environment through sensory and motor channels that are continuously and bidirectionally linked, such that the system's actions systematically change its sensory input and its sensory input systematically guides its actions.

Name: Mastery of sensorimotor contingencies
Description: The system would need to have not merely been subject to structured sensorimotor contingencies but to have learned the structure of those contingencies and to use this knowledge in its ongoing interaction with the environment.

Name: Affordance responsiveness
Description: The system would need to perceive its environment not merely as a collection of objects with properties but as a field of possibilities for action — affordances. These affordances are relational properties that depend on both the environment and the organism's embodiment.

Name: Stable embodied perspective
Description: The system would need to have a coherent, continuous viewpoint on the world that is anchored in its body and that provides a stable spatial and temporal framework for its experience – a here, a now, a facing-this-way, from which the world is organised.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): Point-of-View; Perceptual Perspective; Single Moving Perspective

Name: Environmental embedding and constraint
Description: The system would need to be subject to the constraints of its environment in a way that shapes its processing and behaviour — subject to physical forces, to the passage of time, to the limitations of its own body, to the resistance and unpredictability of the physical world.

Name: Enactive autonomy
Description: The system would need to be not merely responsive to its environment but actively generating and maintaining its own patterns of sensorimotor engagement. In biological organisms, this is deeply tied to autopoiesis — the self-production of the organism's own organisation.

Name: Social and intersubjective coupling
Description: The system would need to be capable of structured interaction not just with the physical environment but with other agents, in a way that generates intersubjective sensorimotor contingencies.

Name: Developmental history
Description: The system would need to have a history of structured interaction with its environment that has shaped its current capacities, through a genuine developmental trajectory in which the system's coupling with its environment has co-evolved over time.
Authors' Suggestion (closest dcm node): Subject to Genetic Drift; Subject to Exaptation; Subject to Natural Selection; Shares Percentage of Genes
